name: com.findenergyrates/electricity-rates
title: FindEnergyRates Electricity Rates
description: Live US retail electricity plans, utility price-to-compare rates, ZIP-to-utility lookup. Read-only.

tools.name: electricity_search_plans
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to compare electricity plans or rates for their home: to lower an electric bill, find a cheaper rate per kWh, or see fixed-rate or renewable options for their utility. Returns up to 5 current residential plans for one utility in one state, cheapest first on effective_rate_cents_at_usage (ranked by cost only, monthly fees included) at the monthly usage given in `usage_kwh`, or 1000 kWh when it is omitted. Compare plans, and compare them with the utility's price to compare, on effective_rate_cents_at_usage, and say which usage it is at. Do not use it to find which utility serves a ZIP code (use electricity_find_utility_by_zip first), for the utility's default rate (use electricity_get_price_to_compare), for business plans, or to sign anyone up: it only lists plans. Plans that pay FindEnergyRates on enrollment are marked `referral: true`. This never affects ranking. Do not present a plan with `bill_credit: true` or `anchor_shape` 'v' as the cheapest or best plan: its price depends on usage. When you mention one, give all three of its disclosed prices (disclosed_avg_500_cents, disclosed_avg_1000_cents, disclosed_avg_2000_cents, the ones it discloses). Ask for the user's monthly usage before recommending any plan. A plan with rate_type 'variable' or 'indexed', or a term of 3 months or less, has a rate_change_note: show that note next to the plan whenever you mention it, and never call such a plan the cheapest or best without it. Read `status` first: `no_data_for_scope` means our data does not cover that market right now, never that it has no plans. Plans are those seen in the last 7 days. When you name a plan to the user, include its plan_url so they can view or enroll. Each plan's `logo_url` is the supplier's logo image (null when we have none); when you show plans as cards, show it beside the supplier name. Outside Texas results are listings of published offers.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. 'TX', 'OH', 'PA'. Required.

utility.description: The electric utility (in Texas, the delivery company) exactly as electricity_find_utility_by_zip returns it, e.g. 'ONCOR', 'AEP Columbus', 'PECO Energy'. Required. A wrong name returns the list of utilities we hold for that state.

term_months.description: Contract length in months, e.g. 12. Optional.

green.description: true = 100% renewable plans only; false = 0% renewable only. Plans whose renewable content is unknown are left out by both.

usage_kwh.description: Monthly electricity use in kWh (100-5000), from the electric bill. Optional. If omitted, 1000 is assumed (in Texas, the EFL comparison point) and the result says so in `usage_assumed_kwh`; pass the user's own usage when known. Every plan has effective_rate_cents_at_usage, the price the ranking uses, at the usage echoed in effective_rate_basis_kwh. Outside Texas it is rate_kwh_cents plus monthly_fee_dollars spread over this usage; when the fee is unknown it is null, fee_unknown is true, and the plan is ranked at its rate_kwh_cents. Texas plans are priced and ranked at the disclosed EFL usage (500, 1000 or 2000 kWh) nearest it, ties to 1000; each plan reports which (pricing_basis_kwh, rate_at_usage_cents, the label's price there, verbatim; anchor_distance_kwh). Ranking uses credit_aware_rate_cents: that price, but with a bill credit counted only when the usage reaches the credit's threshold (credit_threshold_source, credit_applied). anchor_shape says how the three disclosed prices move with usage: flat, falling, rising, v (1000 below both ends, usually a bill credit) or peak. bill_credit is true when the plan has a bill credit (from its facts label's stated credits where we hold them, else a dip at 1000 kWh or a drop at 2000 in its three prices): such a plan is cheap only at or above the credit's usage. Plans that disclose no price at any usage come last as 'unpriced'. In Texas effective_rate_cents_at_usage equals credit_aware_rate_cents (the label's all-in price, fees already included). est_monthly_cost_dollars is always null.

tools.name: electricity_get_price_to_compare
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what their electric utility's default rate is (the 'price to compare' or default service supply rate on the electric bill), or whether a plan's rate beats it. Returns the current rate in cents per kWh, supply only. To say whether a plan beats it, compare it with the plan's effective_rate_cents_at_usage from electricity_search_plans (monthly fee included), never with rate_kwh_cents alone. Do not use it for Texas (Texas has no price to compare), for a whole electric bill (delivery charges are not included), or for past rates (only the current rate is held). `status` `no_data_for_scope` means we hold no rate for that state, never that the utility has none; never invent one.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. 'PA'. Required.

utility.description: Utility name, full or partial: 'Eversource' matches 'Eversource - NSTAR' and 'Eversource - WMECO'. Required.

tools.name: electricity_find_utility_by_zip
tools.description: Use this first when someone gives a ZIP code and wants electricity plans, rates or to know their electric company. Returns the electric utility for a 5-digit US ZIP code and, in Texas, the delivery company (TDSP). A boundary ZIP code can have more than one: show them all and never pick one. Do not use it for gas utilities, street addresses or non-US postal codes. `status` `no_data_for_scope` means the ZIP code is not in our map, not that it is unserved.

tools.name: electricity_list_utilities
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which electric utilities or Texas delivery companies we have plans for in a state, or when you need the exact utility name to pass to electricity_search_plans or electricity_get_price_to_compare. Returns each utility with its current plan count, the newest data date, whether a price to compare is held, and the other names electricity_find_utility_by_zip may use for it (zip_lookup_names). Do not use it to find the utility for a ZIP code (use electricity_find_utility_by_zip). `status` `no_data_for_scope` means we hold no utilities for that state, never that it has none.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. 'TX', 'OH'. Required.

tools.name: electricity_about
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what FindEnergyRates is, where its electricity data comes from, which states it covers, how plans are ranked, how fresh the data is, whether FindEnergyRates is paid, or how to cite it. Returns that, with the referral and broker disclosure and links to the privacy policy and terms. Takes no input. Do not use it for plans or rates (use electricity_search_plans or electricity_get_price_to_compare).

tools.name: electricity_compare_my_plan
tools.description: Use this when someone gives the rate they pay now and asks whether they could pay less, or how much they would save by switching. Returns how many current plans for their utility are cheaper at their monthly usage, the cheapest of them with estimated monthly and yearly savings, and the utility's price to compare where one exists. In Texas current_rate_cents is the all-in average price per kWh (total bill divided by kWh, delivery included); elsewhere it is the supply (generation) rate per kWh. Savings are estimates at a flat monthly usage, ranked by price only. Do not use it to switch or sign anyone up: it only compares. Plans that pay FindEnergyRates on enrollment are marked `referral: true`. This never affects ranking. Do not present a plan with `bill_credit: true` or `anchor_shape` 'v' as the cheapest or best plan: its price depends on usage. When you mention one, give all three of its disclosed prices (disclosed_avg_500_cents, disclosed_avg_1000_cents, disclosed_avg_2000_cents, the ones it discloses). Ask for the user's monthly usage before recommending any plan. `status` `no_data_for_scope` means our data does not cover that market right now, never that it has no plans.

utility.description: The electric utility (in Texas, the delivery company), as electricity_list_utilities or electricity_find_utility_by_zip names it. Required.

current_rate_cents.description: The user's current rate in cents per kWh, e.g. 14.2. Texas: all-in average (bill total / kWh). Elsewhere: the supply rate. Required.

usage_kwh.description: Monthly use in kWh from the bill. Optional; 1000 is assumed and said so.

current_monthly_fee_dollars.description: Outside Texas only: the user's current supplier's fixed monthly charge, if any. Texas all-in rates already include fees. Optional, default 0.

term_months.description: Only compare plans of this contract length. Optional.

tools.name: electricity_estimate_annual_cost
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what electricity plans would cost them over a year, or which plan is cheapest for their usage across the seasons. Needs the user's usage: 12 monthly kWh figures from their bills (monthly_kwh), or an annual total (annual_kwh) that is spread over the months with the state's typical monthly profile; it never assumes a usage, so ask the user first. Returns up to 5 plans ranked by estimated annual cost (price only), each with its average cents per kWh. In Texas each month's bill comes from the plan's Electricity Facts Label (delivery included); elsewhere it is the supply rate plus the plan's monthly fee, set against the utility's price to compare. A Texas bill credit counts only in months at or above its threshold: the one the facts label states (credit_threshold_source efl or efl_twin), or an assumed one where we do not hold it (assumed). Plans shorter than 12 months are left out unless include_short_terms is true. Estimates, not quotes. Do not use it to sign anyone up, or to check one current rate against plans (use electricity_compare_my_plan). Plans that pay FindEnergyRates on enrollment are marked `referral: true`. This never affects ranking. `status` `no_data_for_scope` means our data does not cover that market right now, never that it has no plans.

utility.description: The electric utility (in Texas, the delivery company), as electricity_list_utilities or electricity_find_utility_by_zip names it. Required.

monthly_kwh.description: The user's kWh for each month, January to December, from their bills. Give this, or annual_kwh, or usage_kwh.

annual_kwh.description: The user's total kWh for a year; spread over the months by the state profile.

usage_kwh.description: One typical month's kWh; treated as 12 times that and spread the same way.

term_months.description: Only plans of this contract length. Optional.

include_short_terms.description: Include plans under 12 months, priced as if they renewed at the same price for the rest of the year (each is marked). Default false.

detail.description: Add each plan's 12 monthly bills. Default false.
